title: Ordered convolution word product rule for counit derivations
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a commutative unital $k$-algebra. Let $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_k C$ and $\varepsilon:C\to k$ be unital $k$-algebra maps satisfying coassociativity and the two counit identities $(\varepsilon\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=\mathrm{id}_C$, under the canonical tensor identifications. For $k$-linear maps $a,b:C\to k$ set $a*b=(a\otimes b)\Delta$, with the product in $k$ understood. Let $r\geq0$ and let $v_1,\ldots,v_r:C\to k$ be $k$-linear maps with
$$v_i(cd)=\varepsilon(c)v_i(d)+v_i(c)\varepsilon(d)\qquad(c,d\in C).$$
For a subset $T=\{i_1<\cdots<i_s\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ write $W_T=v_{i_1}*\cdots*v_{i_s}$, with $W_\varnothing=\varepsilon$. For every $m\geq1$ and every $c_1,\ldots,c_m\in C$ one has
$$W_{\{1,\ldots,r\}}(c_1\cdots c_m)=\sum_{f:\{1,\ldots,r\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}}\ \prod_{j=1}^m W_{f^{-1}(j)}(c_j).$$
The order in each $W_{f^{-1}(j)}$ is the inherited increasing order. No finite-generation, antipode or cocommutativity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section 11e, 11.24--11.26, printed pp.216--218, and Lemma 11.27, printed p.218: agent-extracted ordered product-rule prerequisite for the evaluation-at-the-identity calculation, not a separately stated lemma in Milne.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-convolution-linear-map-algebra] with $R=B=k$ and the stated coalgebra $(C,\Delta,\varepsilon)$. Its hypotheses are exactly linearity, coassociativity and the two counit identities assumed here. Thus convolution is associative with unit $\varepsilon$; in particular $a*\varepsilon=\varepsilon*a=a$ for every linear functional $a$. Ordered words can therefore be evaluated with left association, and adjoining a last index $t$ gives $W_{T\cup\{t\}}=W_T*v_t$ whenever every element of $T$ is smaller than $t$, including $T=\varnothing$. We prove the claimed formula simultaneously for all $m\geq1$ and all inputs by induction on the word length $r$. For $r=0$ there is one function from the empty set to $\{1,\ldots,m\}$; the equality reduces to $\varepsilon(c_1\cdots c_m)=\prod_j\varepsilon(c_j)$, which follows by repeated multiplicativity of the assumed algebra map $\varepsilon$.

source.place: Section 11e, 11.24–11.26, printed pp.216–218, and Lemma 11.27, printed p.218; agent-written ordered convolution calculation for evaluation at the identity.

proof.text:
First expand the assumed binary rule for any one of the $v_i$. For $m\geq1$ it gives
$$v_i(y_1\cdots y_m)=\sum_{j=1}^m v_i(y_j)\prod_{\ell\ne j}\varepsilon(y_\ell).$$
Indeed, for $m=1$ this is the identity $v_i(y_1)=v_i(y_1)$. If it holds for $P=y_1\cdots y_m$, then $v_i(Py_{m+1})=\varepsilon(P)v_i(y_{m+1})+v_i(P)\varepsilon(y_{m+1})$. Substituting $\varepsilon(P)=\prod_{\ell=1}^m\varepsilon(y_\ell)$ and the induction formula gives respectively the new $j=m+1$ summand and all old summands. This is an elementary induction using precisely the binary rule in the statement.

source.place: Section 11e, 11.24–11.26, printed pp.216–218, and Lemma 11.27, printed p.218; agent-written ordered convolution calculation for evaluation at the identity.

proof.text:
For the induction step from $r$ to $r+1$, fix $m\geq1$ and $c_1,\ldots,c_m$. The tensor product is generated by pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so write, with finite index sets $A_j$,
$$\Delta(c_j)=\sum_{\alpha\in A_j}x_{j,\alpha}\otimes y_{j,\alpha}.$$
Scalar coefficients have been absorbed into $x_{j,\alpha}$. For a tuple $\boldsymbol\alpha\in\prod_j A_j$ abbreviate $x_j=x_{j,\alpha_j}$ and $y_j=y_{j,\alpha_j}$. Multiplicativity of the assumed map $\Delta$, the tensor-algebra identity $(x\otimes y)(x'\otimes y')=xx'\otimes yy'$, and finite distributivity give
$$\Delta(c_1\cdots c_m)=\sum_{\boldsymbol\alpha}(\prod_j x_j)\otimes(\prod_j y_j).$$
Consequently, by the definition of convolution and linearity,
$$(W_{\{1,\ldots,r\}}*v_{r+1})(\prod_j c_j)=\sum_{\boldsymbol\alpha}W_{\{1,\ldots,r\}}(\prod_j x_j)\,v_{r+1}(\prod_j y_j).$$
Every sum here is finite, even when $C$ is infinite-dimensional.

source.place: Section 11e, 11.24–11.26, printed pp.216–218, and Lemma 11.27, printed p.218; agent-written ordered convolution calculation for evaluation at the identity.

proof.text:
Apply the induction hypothesis for the length-$r$ prefix to each $\prod_j x_j$ in step 3, and apply step 2 to $v_{r+1}(\prod_j y_j)$. For a function $f:\{1,\ldots,r\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$ put $T_\ell=f^{-1}(\ell)$. Distributing the resulting finite sums, the expression in step 3 becomes
$$\sum_f\sum_{j=1}^m\sum_{\boldsymbol\alpha} W_{T_j}(x_j)v_{r+1}(y_j)\prod_{\ell\ne j}\bigl(W_{T_\ell}(x_\ell)\varepsilon(y_\ell)\bigr).$$
Only scalar factors in the commutative field $k$ have been rearranged. No convolution factors have been exchanged. The induction hypothesis is applied to arbitrary inputs $x_j\in C$, not just to generators or augmentation-ideal elements.

source.place: Section 11e, 11.24–11.26, printed pp.216–218, and Lemma 11.27, printed p.218; agent-written ordered convolution calculation for evaluation at the identity.

proof.text:
For fixed $(f,j)$, distributivity over the independent finite sets $A_\ell$ factors its inner sum as
$$\left(\sum_{\alpha_j\in A_j}W_{T_j}(x_{j,\alpha_j})v_{r+1}(y_{j,\alpha_j})\right)\prod_{\ell\ne j}\left(\sum_{\alpha_\ell\in A_\ell}W_{T_\ell}(x_{\ell,\alpha_\ell})\varepsilon(y_{\ell,\alpha_\ell})\right).$$
By the defining convolution formula these factors are $(W_{T_j}*v_{r+1})(c_j)$ and $(W_{T_\ell}*\varepsilon)(c_\ell)$. The unit identity from [lem-sfb-convolution-linear-map-algebra] identifies the latter with $W_{T_\ell}(c_\ell)$. Step 1 identifies the former with $W_{T_j\cup\{r+1\}}(c_j)$, since $r+1$ is larger than every old index; if $T_j$ is empty, this says $\varepsilon*v_{r+1}=v_{r+1}$. Thus the summand indexed by $(f,j)$ is exactly the required product for the assignment extending $f$ by assigning $r+1$ to $j$.

source.place: Section 11e, 11.24–11.26, printed pp.216–218, and Lemma 11.27, printed p.218; agent-written ordered convolution calculation for evaluation at the identity.

proof.text: Every function $g:\{1,\ldots,r+1\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$ has a unique pair $(f,j)$ as in step 5: $f$ is its restriction to $\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and $j=g(r+1)$. Conversely this prescription extends every pair uniquely. Reindexing the finite sum by this explicit bijection proves the length-$r+1$ formula and completes the induction. The only ordering operation was appending the greatest index to a fiber; hence the inherited order in every $W_{g^{-1}(\ell)}$ is preserved. No antipode, cocommutativity, characteristic restriction or finite generation was used.
